evidence.pass: All edges verified: messages-page→notifications-service expects {unreadCount: number} which notifications-service declares via getUnreadCount()->Promise<number>. notifications-page→notifications-service expects {notifications: INotification[], hasMore: boolean} which matches listNotifications() return type. notifications-service→messages-cloud sends action:'listNotifications' which notifications-cloud explicitly handles in its switch statement. comments-cloud→notifications-collection calls db.collection('notifications').add() which matches the collection interface. All type signatures are consistent.

All 6 boundary conditions have explicit handlers: BC-001 (idempotency) → FM-NC02 in notifications-collection; BC-002 (pagination) → FM-NF02 in notifications-cloud; BC-003 (stale badge) → FM-NS03 in notifications-service + FM-MP01 in messages-page; BC-004 (dangling targets) → FM-T01 in typings-notification + FM-NK01 in notification-card; BC-005 (anonymous identity) → FM-NF05 in notifications-cloud; BC-006 (quota limits) → FM-CC01 in comments-cloud. No uncovered boundaries.

Dependency chain: ADAPTER (messages-page) → SERVICE (notifications-service) → SERVICE (messages-cloud) → ENTITY (notifications-collection). Each hop is exactly one abstraction level. No ADAPTER→ENTITY bypass. The comments-cloud→notifications-collection edge is SERVICE→ENTITY, also a single-level gap. No warnings.

DFS cycle detection on all edges: no cycles found. The dependency graph is a DAG. Key flows: messages-page→notifications-page (navigation, not a module dependency edge — not in the graph); notifications-page→notifications-service→messages-cloud→notifications-collection (linear chain); comments-cloud→notifications-collection (separate entry point, no back-edges).

All 10 modules have both extension_points and sealed_points declared. Key examples: INotification type is open for new NotificationType enum values, sealed for standard fields. notification-card is open for per-type templates, sealed for card structure. notifications-cloud is open for new notification types, sealed for auth requirement.

All 15 failure modes have complete propagation paths. Example trace — FM-NP02 (pagination network error): notification-card renders inline error → user sees toast → retry via pull-to-refresh. FM-CC01 (notification creation fails): error logged in comments-cloud → comment creation continues → response includes flagged field → frontend ignores notification_failed flag. No failure mode terminates in unhandled panic or silent swallow without explicit justification.

State ownership is unambiguous: notifications-collection owns all notification records (sole writer via cloud functions). notifications-page owns its list state (items, hasMore, cursor). messages-page owns its conversation list and stubUnreadCount. The only shared state is the notifications collection between notifications-cloud and comments-cloud — both are explicitly listed as writers, and the coordination mechanism (CloudBase's built-in document-level concurrency) is implicit in the database layer.

Design follows Douyin two-tier model recommendation from research: Stub entry at top of conversation list → notification feed page. Consistent with research recommendation #1 (adopt Douyin two-tier model). Notification type enum supports comment/reply/like/follow/system as documented in the research (#2). Stub is a UI-level construct not a real user (#1). One deviation from research: Meta's inline module approach was rejected in favor of Douyin's two-tier — this is documented in the trade-off analysis and is a conscious choice documented in the topology notes.

All 15 failure modes across all module specs have at least one test_contract defined. Total test contracts: 15. Each contract specifies scenario, type (UNIT or INTEGRATION), and verifies clause. 4 contracts reference specific boundary conditions (BC-001, BC-002, BC-003, BC-004, BC-005, BC-006). No failure mode lacks a test contract.
